title: HubSpot Gmail Integration Workflows Without Code
summary: HubSpot Gmail integration has two layers: HubSpot's inbox logs emails to contacts, and workflow tools handle what the connection doesn't cover.
body_markdown:
## HubSpot and Gmail Connection Limits and Errors


Two sets of limits decide whether the contact-triggered email keeps running: daily sending caps on the Gmail side and API request allowances on the HubSpot side.


Most errors beyond those come from expired authorization, empty fields and duplicate records. Figures below were checked on 15 November 2026.


### Gmail sending limits and daily caps


**500 emails per day** is where[Google's support page](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22839?hl=en) puts a free Gmail account. Google Workspace is at 2,000. HubSpot Sequences on Professional allow 500 per user, and on Enterprise 1,000 per user, which means Enterprise provides double the sequence capacity per user.


The chart compares the four.


Past 500 new contacts in a day, a free Gmail sender stops delivering, and nothing in the workflow warns you.


Workspace gives the most headroom for a single sender, so anything sending from one shared mailbox belongs there.


### HubSpot API rate limits


Every run of a workflow tool calls HubSpot's API.[Scopious Digital](https://www.scopiousdigital.com/blog/hubspot-api-rate-limits-production) reports daily allowances of **250,000 requests on Free and Starter** , 625,000 on Professional and 1,000,000 on Enterprise.


That's a third-party source, so confirm the numbers against HubSpot's developer documentation before you size anything around them.


One email per new contact costs only a few calls, so a quarter of a million requests is ample.


The allowance runs out when a tool polls HubSpot on a timer or a bulk import pushes thousands of contacts through at once. Prefer a real trigger over polling, and spread imports across days.


### Authorization and expired connection errors


When runs start failing with an authorization error, the Google connection has usually lapsed. A password change, revoked app access or an idle token all invalidate it. Reconnect the Google account inside the workflow tool, then re-run the failed items.


If reconnecting is refused outright, a Workspace admin may be blocking third-party app access. The admin has to allow the app in the Google Admin console; nothing on your side overrides that.


### Fixing empty fields and duplicate HubSpot contacts


A Gmail send action needs a recipient. A contact created without an email address makes the step fail, so add a filter before it that continues only when the email field is known.


Do the same for any merge field in the body, or the message goes out with a blank where the first name should be.


When a contact is updated, re-imported or re-enrolled, it can fire the workflow a second time and send a second email. That is where duplicates come from.


Switch off re-enrollment on the trigger, and have the workflow stamp a property such as "welcome email sent" that the filter checks on every run.
